stem: An investment grew from Rs 10,000 to Rs 12,100 in 2 years with annual compounding. What is the Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Incorrectly estimated sqrt(1.21) as 1.105 instead of exactly 1.10, yielding 10.5%.
Halved the total 2-year rate of 21% by dividing by 2, giving 10.5%, then rounded further to 5%, confusing per-period simple average with CAGR.
Computed the total growth over 2 years as (12100 - 10000)/10000 = 21% without applying the nth-root correction, ignoring the compounding period.

explanation: CAGR applies the formula: CAGR = (End Value / Begin Value)^(1/n) - 1. Here n = 2, End = 12100, Begin = 10000. So CAGR = (1.21)^(1/2) - 1 = 1.10 - 1 = 10%.

explanation_sections.punchline: The nth-root unlocks the per-year rate hidden in the total growth ratio.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: CAGR = (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1. Map givens: PV = 10000, FV = 12100, n = 2. Compute ratio 1.21, take square root = 1.10, subtract 1 to get 10%.
explanation_sections.lesson: CAGR always applies the nth-root; never divide the total percentage growth by n.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Spot that 1.21 = 1.1^2 instantly to avoid a calculator step. Trap: option 4 is the naive total-growth read-off.
